name: pyhctsa
tagline: The most comprehensive time-series feature extraction toolkit in Python
description: pyhctsa is a Python port of MATLAB's hctsa for highly comparative time-series analysis. It gives researchers and data scientists access to thousands of candidate features that can be computed from almost any time series, letting you move past hand-picked summary statistics and instead extract a broad, comparable signature from your data. A FeatureCalculator object initializes the full feature set or a custom YAML-defined subset, and its extract() method turns a collection of unequal-length series into a single N x F pandas dataframe where F is the number of extracted features. The workload is computationally intensive, so pyhctsa ships a LocalDistributor that spreads feature extraction across multiple CPU cores. Individual operations can also be called directly from their modules, and the package includes tutorials to get started quickly.
highlights: Thousands of time-series features ported from MATLAB's hctsa
FeatureCalculator supports the full feature set or custom YAML-defined subsets
Extracts an N x F feature matrix from series of unequal length
LocalDistributor parallelizes feature extraction across multiple CPU cores
Includes step-by-step tutorials and example workflows
curatorNote: hctsa is a standard tool in dynamical-systems research, but until pyhctsa its depth was locked inside MATLAB. Bringing thousands of comparable time-series features to open-source Python is a real contribution, and it is remarkable that the port sits at only ~120 stars — a TLDR Tech data/ML pick that deserves a wider audience.
